# OrgPath Governance Golden Path

This is the **one walkthrough** that runs the OrgPath wedge end-to-end on a
single coherent sample tenant — the path a design partner runs on their own desk
*before* a pilot ever touches a real directory.

It takes Active Directory facts, derives canonical OrgPath facets, finds the
devices that are missing them, classifies the resulting drift, and emits a
**signed, auditor-grade evidence bundle** — in four commands, with **no live AD,
no Azure tenant, and no API keys**. Everything is read-only or dry-run by
default.

> **Two quickstarts, two jobs.** The [10-minute
> quickstart](quickstart.qmd) produces a SCuBA *compliance* drift report. This
> golden path is the *identity-governance* story: the OrgPath differentiator,
> from directory to signed evidence. They don't overlap.

Prerequisites: Python 3.10+, git.

## What you'll prove

| Stage | Command | The claim it substantiates |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `uiao orgtree assess` | AD attributes deterministically map to a governed, schema-validated OrgPath codebook. |
| 2 | `uiao orgtree inventory` | We can find every enrolled device *missing* OrgPath and propose a backfill from a source of truth. |
| 3 | `uiao orgtree govern` | Identity gaps re-surface as classified drift, with halt-on-critical and dry-run safety. |
| 4 | `uiao ir orgtree-readiness-bundle` | The whole thing terminates in a **signed** bundle + **OSCAL** Assessment Results an auditor accepts. |

## Run it now (the impatient path)

```bash
git clone https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao && cd uiao
pip install -e .
examples/orgtree/golden-path/run.sh
```

`run.sh` executes all four stages against the committed sample data in
`examples/orgtree/golden-path/` and writes every artifact to `./out`
(gitignored). The rest of this page walks each stage so you understand what you
just saw. The data dictionary — what every sample record seeds and the
known-answer it produces — is in the
[dataset README](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/examples/orgtree/golden-path/README.md).

---

## Stage 1 — `assess`: Active Directory → OrgPath facets

The identity plane. `assess` reads AD user objects and derives each user's
OrgPath facet values through a tenant-tunable AD→facet mapping, validating every
derived value against the codebook (UIAO_151).

```bash
uiao orgtree assess \
  --from-export examples/orgtree/golden-path/ad-users.json \
  --out out/assignments.json
```

```
OrgPath assessment — 5 user(s) from AD
  Facets derived : 37
  Findings       : 13
Assignments written to out/assignments.json
```

The five sample users span the real cases: three map cleanly, `carol.unknown`
(department "Astrophysics", title "Wizard") has **no codebook alias** and surfaces
as findings, and `svc.backup` is derived as a service account from its
`userAccountControl` flag. A finding is an AD value the codebook doesn't
recognize — exactly the input a tenant uses to tune its mapping or fix its
directory. The per-user assignment looks like:

```json
{
  "target_id": "CN=alice.eng,OU=Engineering,OU=Users,DC=contoso,DC=com",
  "target_type": "user",
  "facet_values": {
    "region": "EASTUS", "department": "Engineering", "role": "Engineer",
    "classification": "Employee", "hire_date": "2021-01-15",
    "account_type": "Standard"
  },
  "findings": [ ... ]
}
```

> **Live AD?** Drop `--from-export` and pass `--ldap-server` / `--base-dn` for a
> live read. Everything downstream is identical.

---

## Stage 2 — `inventory`: which devices are missing OrgPath?

The device plane. Identity facets are only useful if your *devices* carry them —
that's what makes Entra dynamic groups and Intune/Arc policy targeting
deterministic. `inventory` reads already-enrolled devices across Entra (Graph
`onPremisesExtensionAttributes`) and Arc (ARM `tags`), classifies each one's
OrgPath capture status, and proposes a backfill from a source of truth.

```bash
uiao orgtree inventory \
  --devices-export examples/orgtree/golden-path/entra-devices.json \
  --machines-export examples/orgtree/golden-path/arc-machines.json \
  --owner-map examples/orgtree/golden-path/owner-map.json \
  --snapshot-out out/inventory-snapshot.json \
  --worklist-out out/worklist.json
```

```
OrgPath inventory — 6 device(s) (Entra 4, Arc 2)
  Captured (complete) : 0
  Partial             : 3
  Absent (no OrgPath) : 3
  Needs backfill      : 6
    proposal resolved : 1
    unresolved        : 5 (no source match — manual review)
```

`WS-HR-03` is **absent** but its registered owner `dana.hr` is in the owner-map
with a full facet set, so its backfill is **fully resolved**. The Arc machines
have no registered owner and no `--asset-map`, so they bucket for manual review.
That spread — resolved, partial, unresolved — is the point: it's the honest
output of a partial backfill source, and the `worklist.json` is the operator's
to-do list. This step **writes nothing**; it emits a `worklist.json` plus a
`govern`-compatible snapshot of current state for stage 3.

---

## Stage 3 — `govern`: gaps become classified drift

Feed the current-state snapshot to one governance pass. The runtime
(UIAO_163 / UIAO_174) runs the drift engine against the codebook and emits one
telemetry event per finding.

```bash
uiao orgtree govern out/inventory-snapshot.json \
  --detection-only \
  --out out/drift-report.json
```

```
OrgPath governance pass — mode=detection-only, dry_run=True, snapshot=snap-...
  Drift findings : 100
    P1 : 6
    P2 : 40
    P3 : 54
  Planned ops    : 0
  Remediated ops : 0
  Telemetry      : 102 events
  HALTED — critical finding present; remediation suppressed.
```

Two properties to notice, because they're the difference between a governance
*product* and a diff script:

- **`dry_run=True` and `Planned ops: 0`** — detection only. The pass classifies
  and reports; it plans and writes nothing. Drop `--detection-only` to wire the
  canonical Phase 5 adapters (ADR-084) and see *planned* operations — still
  write-free until a transport is injected and `--no-dry-run` is set.
- **`HALTED`** — a critical (P1) finding stops remediation. Fail-closed is the
  default for a tool that can mutate a directory.

The exact severity counts track the canonical codebook and will move as it
evolves; the shape (drift present, criticals present, halted, dry-run) is the
contract.

---

## Stage 4 — signed evidence bundle + OSCAL

Terminate the path in something an auditor accepts: a signed bundle and OSCAL
Assessment Results. This stage takes an AD survey — we reuse the larger
committed synthetic forest — and emits the evidence artifacts.

```bash
uiao ir orgtree-readiness-bundle examples/orgtree/synthetic-forest-export.json \
  --out-dir out/bundle \
  --oscal-out out/oscal \
  --insecure-dev-key
```

```
OrgTree Readiness bundle written to out/bundle
  Users : 50   Groups : 20   Computers : 30   Servers : 15
  Hash  : 5e6be666...    Sig : 1229d39c...
OSCAL evidence written to out/oscal/orgtree-evidence.json
```

You get four artifacts: `bundle.json` (schema-validated), `bundle.hash`
(SHA-256), `bundle.sig` (HMAC-SHA256), and `oscal/orgtree-evidence.json` (OSCAL
Assessment Results). The signature lets a consumer verify the bundle wasn't
altered after issuance.

> **`--insecure-dev-key` is for this offline demo only.** A real run sets the
> `UIAO_BUNDLE_HMAC_KEY` environment variable and drops the flag, so the
> signature is bound to a key you control. With the flag, the signature offers
> no security — it only lets the demo run without a configured key.

---

## What you just demonstrated

From a fresh clone, with no tenant and no keys, you took Active Directory facts
to a **signed, OSCAL-shaped evidence bundle** — through deterministic OrgPath
derivation, device-gap inventory, and classified, fail-closed, dry-run-safe
drift. That is the OrgPath wedge, end to end, on one desk.

The next step is the same path against a real `--from-export` (or live
`--ldap-server`) — the dry-run-by-default posture makes that a low-risk pilot.

## Reproducibility

The pipeline is pinned by `tests/test_orgpath_golden_path.py`, which runs all
four stages against the committed sample data in CI and asserts the structural
invariants above — so this walkthrough can't silently rot as the CLI evolves.
